newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower as KEPCO falls.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower as KEPCO falls.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed lower on Thursday as a profit-taking in electricity-monopoly KEPCO led a fall among blue chips, dealers said.
But they said buying interest remained strong in second-tier shares and some small-capitalised stocks.
The composite stock index shed 3.84 points to provisionally close at 797.61. Losers slightly led gainers by 419 to 392.

"Large-cap shares were in consolidation, sparked by falls in KEPCO," said Kwon Oh-seung of Samsung Securities. "But recently falling interest rates backed by improving liquidity will limit further sharp declines on the index."
Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds hit a low of 12.05, falling from Wednesday's close of 12.18 and its year high of 12.58 on August 22.

KEPCO, heavily weighted on the index, lost 600 won to 27,800. The shares have risen on brisk local buying ahead of the expansion of the foreign stock holdling limit from October 1. Samsung Electronics lost 600 won to 59,500 and POSCO dropped 1,000 won to 59,500.
Cha Hee-guan of Sunkyong Securities said the market fell more steeply in the afternoon on news that U.S. warplanes were set to strike against targets in Iraq.
Brokers said concerns about heavy selling from margin account holders due in mid-September put a dent on the market.
The bourse later revised its closing index to 797.57, down 3.88 points. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
